beats: A man threw giant parties every weekend, hoping one woman would wander in!
It's 1922, and his neighbor Nick has no idea who he really is.
This is The Great Gatsby, by F. Scott Fitzgerald.
Five years earlier, a young officer named Jay Gatsby fell for a girl named Daisy, then went to war.
While he was gone, she married rich Tom Buchanan.
So Gatsby got rich, bought a mansion across the bay, and stared at the green light on her dock!
When she never showed, he had Nick invite her over for tea.
Soon they were seeing each other, and the parties stopped.
Then, in a sweltering hotel room, Gatsby told Tom that Daisy never loved him!
Daisy said she'd loved them both.
Driving Gatsby's yellow car home, Daisy hit and killed Tom's mistress, Myrtle, and didn't stop.
Gatsby said he'd take the blame.
Tom told Myrtle's husband whose car it was.
The next day, Gatsby finally used his pool, and the husband shot him in it.
Hundreds came to his parties, but almost nobody came to his funeral.
And the one guest he'd thrown them all for didn't even send a flower!
